question: What is volatility risk, and why do stock prices fluctuate even when companies aren't failing?
reference_answer: Even when companies aren’t in danger of failing, their stock price may fluctuate up or down.  Large company stocks as a group, for example, have lost money on average about one out of every three years.  Market fluctuations can be unnerving to some investors.  A stock’s price can be affected by factors inside the company, such as a faulty product, or by events the company has no control over, such as political or market events.
title: What is Risk? | Investor.gov
